sentences.text: Present: Mr. R.P.Singh, Deputy Advocate General, for the appellants.
Mr. Athrav Sharma, Advocate, for the respondent.
of Cmp No.14772 of 2023
List after two weeks, as prayed for.
Reply, if any, be filed in the meantime.
rt CMP No. 14773 of 2023
The present application has been filed for modification of the order dated 18.08.2023, passed by this Court.
It has been asserted that this Court had ordered the payment of compensation; however, the compensation cannot be determined without acquiring the land.
The decree is un-executable because there is a direction to pay compensation without any direction to assess the amount as per Land Acquisition Act.
The judgment and decree are required to be stayed without depositing of the compensation.
The deposit of compensation would amount to implementation of the judgment and decree without following the due process of law.

Hence, it was prayed that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Trial Court and affirmed by the learned First Appellate Court be stayed without the condition of deposit of the compensation amount.
.

The Court may issue direction to assess the compensation in case dismissal of the appeal, hence the application.
of
No reply is intended to be filed.
Heard.
This Court had noticed on 18.08.2023, rt that the State cannot trespass into the property of the citizen without payment of the compensation.
Reliance was placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vidya Devi vs. The State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors. 2020 (2) SCC 569.

entities.text: Vidya Devi vs. The State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors. 2020 (2) SCC 569
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in order to balance equities, it was ordered that execution of the judgments and decrees passed by the learned Courts below shall remain stayed subject to the deposit of the compensation.
Now the State is taking up a plea that it is not permissible to deposit the compensation without initiating the process under Land Acquisition Act.

Since the equities cannot be balanced in view of the plea taken by the State that the determination of the compensation is not possible, therefore, the only course left is to return the land to the person from whom it was taken as per the judgment and decree passed by the learned Trial Court as affirmed by the learned First Appellate Court.
This will also not harm the State as the land can always be returned to it, if .

Therefore, order dated 18.08.2023, is vacated and the CMP No. 14584 of 2020 is ordered to rt be dismissed.
